DECISION AND OPINION ON REVIEW 
 
 
Timely Petition for Review having been filed by the Respondent herein and notice given 
to all parties, the Commission, after considering the issues of accident, causal connection, medical 
expenses, temporary total disability, and permanent partial disability, and being advised of the 
facts and law, affirms and adopts the Decision of the Arbitrator, which is attached hereto and made 
a part hereof.   
 
 
IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that the Decision of the 
Arbitrator filed July 21, 2025, is hereby affirmed and adopted. 
 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that the Respondent pay to 
Petitioner interest under §19(n) of the Act, if any. 
 
 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that the Respondent shall have 
credit for all amounts paid, if any, to or on behalf of the Petitioner on account of said accidental 
injury.

An Application for Adjustment of Claim was filed in this matter, and a Notice of Hearing was mailed to each 
party.  The matter was heard by the Honorable Dennis O'Brien, Arbitrator of the Commission, in the city of 
Peoria, on May 22, 2025.  After reviewing all of the evidence presented, the Arbitrator hereby makes findings 
on the disputed issues checked below, and attaches those findings to this document.  
 
DISPUTED ISSUES 
 
A. 
 Was Respondent operating under and subject to the Illinois Workers' Compensation or Occupational

B. 
 Was there an employee-employer relationship? 
C.

FINDINGS 
 
On October 15, 2018, Respondent was operating under and subject to the provisions of the Act.   
 
On this date, an employee-employer relationship did exist between Petitioner and Respondent.   
 
On this date, Petitioner did sustain an accident that arose out of and in the course of employment. 
 
Timely notice of this accident was given to Respondent. 
 
Petitioner's current condition of ill-being is causally related to the accident. 
 
In the year preceding the injury, Petitioner earned $46,800.00; the average weekly wage was $900.00. 
 
On the date of accident, Petitioner was 51 years of age, married with 0 dependent children. 
 
Petitioner has received all reasonable and necessary medical services.   
 
Respondent has not paid all appropriate charges for all reasonable and necessary medical services. 
 
Respondent shall be given a credit of $0 for TTD, $0 for TPD, $0 for maintenance, and $0 for other benefits, 
for a total credit of $0. 
 
Respondent is entitled to a credit of $51,693.46  under Section 8(j) of the Act. 
 
 
ORDER 
 
   Petitioner suffered an accident on October 15, 2018,  which arose out of and in the course of his employment by 
Respondent.   
   Petitioner’s current medical condition of ill-being,  severe medial compartment wear of the left knee, aggravated 
by the fall of October 15, 2018, is casually related to the accident of April 3, 2017.   
   Petitioner was temporarily totally disabled as a result of the accident of April 3, 2017 from November 17, 2020, to 
January 10, 2021, a period of 7 6/7 weeks.   
   The medical bills contained in Petitioner’s Exhibit 12 are for medical treatment claimed to be related to the  
   accident of April 3, 2017 as well as the accident of October 15, 2018.   
• 
Medical charges on pages 2 through 6 and the charges of June 14, 2017 on page 7 are found to related to 
the medical conditions caused by the accident of April 3, 2017, and are not the responsibility of Respondent 
in this case. 
• 
The other medical charges on page 7 are not related to either the accident of April 3, 2017 or the accident 
of October 15, 2018, and are not the responsibility of Respondent in this case. 
• 
The charges on pages page 18 have no medical records to support their being related to this accident and 
are not the responsibility of Respondent. 
• 
The charges on pages 8 through 17, charges of May 16, 2019 on page 21, and charges of May 16, 2019, 
January 20, 2020, and May 21, 2020 on page 22, are found to be related to the accident of October 15, 2018, 
and are the responsibility of Respondent in this case.  
• 
The charges on pages 23 through 29 are for two surgeries performed on November 17, 2020, the right knee 
meniscal surgery that is the subject matter of 17 WC 017272, and the left total knee replacement surgery 
that is the subject of this case. The charges do no reflect which surgery each individual charge is related to. 
26IWCC0134

3 
 
All of said charges are related to either one, the other, or both surgeries and post-operative care. These 
charges are held to be the responsibility of Respondent in both cases, but these awards are not intended to 
result in the same charge being paid twice, but for payment of a charge in one case to serve as credit 
towards the award in the companion case as well. 
 
   The Arbitrator finds that all of the bills introduced into evidence in Petitioner’s Exhibit 12 which are described 
above as being related to Petitioner’s left knee injury of October 15, 2018, are reasonable and were necessitated 
to treat or cure Petitioner’s injuries suffered in this accident, and are to be paid pursuant to Sections 8(a) and 8.2 
of the Act. 
   Petitioner sustained permanent partial disability to the extent of 35% loss of use of his left leg pursuant to §8(e) 
of the Act. Respondent is entitled to credit of 20% loss of use of the left leg towards said 35% loss of use, due to 
the prior left leg injury of January 22, 2008 and the settlement approved on March 23, 2009. (RX 3) 
 
RULES REGARDING APPEALS  Unless a party files a Petition for Review within 30 days after receipt of this decision, 
and perfects a review in accordance with the Act and Rules, then this decision shall be entered as the decision of 
the Commission.   
 
STATEMENT OF INTEREST RATE  If the Commission reviews this award, interest at the rate set forth on the Notice of 
Decision of Arbitrator shall accrue from the date listed below to the day before the date of payment; however, if 
an employee's appeal results in either no change or a decrease in this award, interest shall not accrue.

 Danny Mayes v. Peoria Public School District 150   19 WC 006115  
 
FINDINGS OF FACT: 
TESTIMONY AT ARBITRATION 
Petitioner 
Petitioner testified that as of the date of arbitration he was working for Respondent at Peoria High School. He 
testified that he graduated from Manuel High School in 1984, and received a bachelor’s degree in management from 
Lincoln Christian University in 2009.  He testified he is certified in HVAC as well as electrical work. He described his 
prior work as involving security, performing maintenance, supervising custodial work, and performing service tech work 
a restaurant chain from Bloomington/Normal, Illinois to Waterloo, Iowa, repairing fryers, grills, walk-in coolers and other 
equipment. Petitioner testified he became employed by Respondent in 2005 at Harrison School, as a custodian, 
subsequently performing several positions in schools throughout the school district, including engineer, custodian, and 
head custodian.  
Petitioner testified that on April 3, 2017, he was working at Woodruff School, where a fashion show was held in 
its main gym.  Following the show, Petitioner said students brought him chairs, he put the chairs on racks, and he would 
then move the racks of chairs down a ramp to the dock area.  He said he would get in front of a rack, and have the rack be 
behind him, so the rack would not drag him down the stairs. While doing this he noticed some pain in his right knee.  
Petitioner stated that he reported the pain to the school secretary that same day.  
Petitioner said Respondent set up his appointments with IWIRC, and he was told by Respondent to go there, 
doing so the following day.  Petitioner testified the office note from IWIRC which stated he first noticed the pain at the 
end of the day when he got into his car was not what he told them, that he did not say that, he told them how it happened, 
and that his pain was 10 out of 10 when it happened.  He said his right knee was examined there, and they said he had a 
right knee strain.  Petitioner testified he received treated at IWIRC on several occasions from April 4, 2017 through April 
26, 2017, being prescribed a brace. He said he had already been taking Tylenol for back pain. He said he did not receive 
any therapy.   Petitioner testified he was sent for an MRI, and he was told he had a torn meniscus.  He was then told to go 
and see his own doctor.  
 Petitioner testified he went to see his primary care physician, Dr. Gilbert, who sent him to Midwest Orthopedics. 
Petitioner said he first saw Dr. Merkley at Midwest Orthopedic regarding his right knee on June 14, 2017. He said he had 
three different doctors he had seen at Midwest Orthopedics. He said he told Dr. Merkley his right leg was still hurting, 
they discussed the results of the MRI, and Dr. Merkley told him he could have elective surgery on his knee, but it was up 
to Petitioner to contact the doctor when he was ready to have surgery. Petitioner testified that he continued to work his 
regular duties full time, using the brace which had been given to him by IWIRC, and continued to take Tylenol and Aleve 
on occasion.  
Petitioner testified that he sustained a second injury to both of his knees, about a year and seven months after he 
last saw Dr. Merkley. He said that on October 15, 2018, while in the boiler room at work, he was climbing a ladder to get 
to the top of the boiler, lost his balance, and fell, landing on the balls of his feet.  At the time of the injury, he had pain in 
his balls of his feet, his hands, his fingers, back, and both of his knees.  Petitioner estimated he fell approximately six feet, 
and had tried to grab the rail with his left hand as he fell. He said his fingers hurt from trying to grab it, his back hurt, and 
his left knee was hurting worse.  
Petitioner initially appeared confused when testifying about a prior knee surgery, saying it was his right knee 
which had previously had surgery, but subsequently both counsel for Petitioner and counsel for Respondent stipulated that 
26IWCC0134

5 
 
it was his left knee operated on in 2008.  Petitioner said that following the 2008 surgery, which was performed by Dr. 
Phillips, he continued to work full duty and was not seen again by any doctors for left knee pain until the October 25, 
2018 injury.  Petitioner said he had settled the 2008 injury for 20% loss of use of the left leg. 
Petitioner testified that following his return to work in 2008 following that left knee surgery, he did not see any 
doctors regarding his knees until the injury on April 3, 2017, when he had right knee pain.  He said he had not had any 
right knee prior to the April 3, 2017 accident. Petitioner said that following the October 15, 2018, injury, his right knee 
pain increased and that the left knee pain was worse than the right knee pain.  Petitioner testified that he saw three 
physicians at Midwest Orthopedic with regard to his knees, that following the second injury, Dr. Merkley referred him to 
Dr. Luetkemeyer to perform the surgeries. Petitioner said he had to have his health insurance pay for the surgeries, he had 
to OSF St. Francis Medical Center for the surgeries, as he believed Dr. Luetkemeyer and several other doctors had lost 
their privileges at OSF St. Francis, so he was referred to Dr. Akeson for the surgery. Dr. Akeson performed a right knee 
arthroscopy and a left total knee replacement on November 17, 2020. 
Petitioner testified the surgeries helped him, and that following the surgeries on his knees, he returned to work full 
duty.  He said he still had numbness in parts of his leg, but he felt 100 percent better, and he can walk a lot better, though 
he still wears his braces. but he continues to have occasional pain in both knees.   
On cross examination, Petitioner testified that he did not remember having surgery on his right knee prior to the 
April 3, 2017 injury. He said if the IWIC records mention a prior right knee surgery in 2016, he did not remember it.  
Petitioner said that at the time of the injury involving the chairs, he was walking down the ramp backwards, 
pulling the rack of chairs. He said you could put about 30 chairs on the rack, and the rack had wheels on it. He said the 
ramp was approximately 10 feet long. He said he did not know if this occurred with the last rack of chairs or if he moved 
additional chairs afterwards. He said he did not fall down or stumble as a result of this accident. When asked what portion 
of the knee was painful at that time, Petitioner described it as being the knee, noting it was nine or ten years prior to the 
trial. He said he did not go to the emergency room that night as the school district does not send people to the emergency 
room, they send people to IWIRC. Petitioner said he did not twist his knee when this occurred, he was walking 
backwards.  
Petitioner again said IWIRC told him he had a torn meniscus, he was not aware that their records reflected he had 
degenerative joint disease that was not consistent with his alleged mechanism of injury.  
Petitioner said Dr. Merkley had previously performed a shoulder surgery on him, which was the result of a 
different workers’ compensation case. He said he did not seek any right knee care from June of 2017 until October of 
2018, if that is what the records indicate. He said he was working full duty for Respondent during that period of time.  
Petitioner agreed that on October 16, 2018 he filled out and signed Respondent Exhibit 10, a Form 45, circling 
portions of a body image on the form indicating the parts of his body he had injured, and on that form the left knee was 
circled, but the right knee was not circled. 
Petitioner testified that after the October 2018 accident, he was treated at IWIRC until February of 2019, and 
during that period of time he was not placed under any work restrictions, continuing to work full duty. He said he 
underwent surgery on both knees the same day, November 17, 2020, three and-a-half years after the first accident of 
April, 2017. He said he waited for the surgery as he could still work, and wanted to work, though he wore his braces and 
took medicine. He said he knew he needed the surgery in 2017, and had it when he did as he was also having surgery on 
his left knee. 
Petitioner said his right knee did pretty well after the surgery, and felt better on the date of arbitration than it had 
prior to the surgery. He said he was still working. He said he was not claiming to have injured the left knee in the incident 
26IWCC0134

6 
 
involving the chairs, he injured it in the ladder incident. He said he did not have left knee pain prior to the ladder incident. 
He said if the IWIRC records of October 2018 indicate a normal left knee examination, no swelling, no tenderness, 
normal range of motion and strength, he would dispute that, as he was in pain.  
Petitioner said his left knee hurt more than his right knee following the ladder incident.  When asked if he asked 
Dr. Gilbert for a referral for the right knee on February 27, 2019, Petitioner said he was not sure. Petitioner was asked if 
he told Dr. Gilbert in February of 2019 that his right knee had been getting worse, especially after driving a lot in a second 
job, saying he was working as a supervisor for a cleaning company, driving to various towns in the Peoria area to check 
out and watch other people work, sometimes pitching in if someone did not show up to work.  
Petitioner said he did not know if the only knee he complained of when seeing Dr. Luetkemeyer in May of 2019 
was his left knee, but said both of them would have been hurting. 
Petitioner testified that in the ladder incident he fell about six feet, landing on his feet.  He said his knees did not 
bang into things, nor did he twist his knees. He said he landed on his feet, on cement. He said when he tried to grab the 
rail while falling, he injured the left hand and fingers. He said he was unaware that the Application for Adjustment of 
Claim listed the right hand and fingers as having been injured. He said that after the ladder fall he finished his shift, sitting 
at his desk.  
Petitioner said he was not sure if he told Dr. Akeson of the April 2017 accident, or of prior right or left knee 
surgeries.  
In regard to claimed periods of temporary total disability, Petitioner said he worked full duty up to the day of his 
November 17, 2020 surgeries, and returned to work at full duty on January 11 or 12, 2021. He said he was not sure when 
he last saw Dr. Akeson, but it was when Dr. Akeson released him to full duty work. He did not believe he had seen Dr. 
Akeson for his knees in the two years prior to the arbitration hearing.  
Petitioner said that he was working for Respondent as of the day of the arbitration hearing, but in a different job.  
He said he was currently a head custodian, while at the time of the ladder accident he was an engineer. He said his current 
job was a promotion, though per the union contract they get paid the same amount.  
Petitioner said the Form 45 forms were not filled out by him, others filled them out. 
On redirect examination Petitioner said his prior knee surgeries were discussed at Dr. Akeson’s deposition. 
 
MEDICAL EVIDENCE 
Pre-Accident records: 
Attached to a Respondent Exhibit 3, an approved settlement contract for a January 22, 2008 accident, which 
included an injury to the left knee and was settled with credit for the left arm, the man as a whole, and 20% loss of use of 
the left leg, were medical records in regard to that left knee injury. (RX 3 p.1-3) 
An operative report of July 24, 2008, noted arthroscopic surgery to the left knee was performed by Dr. Phillips on 
that date. Dr. Phillips found old and new changes of the middle-third of the posterior aspect of the medial meniscus during 
this surgery. He also found degenerative tearing of the central aspect of the lateral meniscus. Both the medial and the 
lateral menisci were debrided back to stable peripheral rims. Articular cartilage was also debrided to smooth the 
patellofemoral, medial, and lateral compartments. (RX 3 p. 6,7) 
IWIRC medical records for August 5, 2008, state that Petitioner had surgery on his left knee on July 24, 2008. 
Surgical scars were noted during an examination on August 20, 2008. Post-operatively, he reported left knee pain from 
26IWCC0134

7 
 
August 8, 2008, through September 10, 2008, to both his physician and to physical therapists. While he continued being 
treated for elbow and back complaints after he had reached MMI for the left knee, he was ready to return to full duty work 
by September 9, 2008. (RX 7 p. 2-7,13,26) 
Petitioner was seen at IWIRC again on December 11, 2008, and no complaints in regard to the left knee are 
included in this record.  It was noted that Petitioner had suffered a contusion of the left knee, that it had resolved, and the 
left knee was at maximum medical improvement. (RX 3 p. 4) 
Petitioner was seen by Physician Assistant (PA) Droege at IWIRC on April 4, 2017, following Respondent’s 
authorization for an evaluation to determine whether his condition was work related, and consistent with his reported 
mechanism of injury, whether treatment was indicated, and, if so, to direct the indicated treatment and determine if 
Petitioner was safe to perform his job requirements. Petitioner gave a history of having injured his right knee injury on 
April 3, 2017, while pulling four racks of chairs, a total of 240 chairs, down a ramp to a dock area. He reported pain rated 
at 10/10 initially, which decreased to 8/10 but worsened to 10/10 when walking up stairs.  He described the pain as 
aching, stabbing, and sore. The history in this office note states that Petitioner did not notice this until the end of the day 
when he got into his car. He said he reported it as they are supposed to do so, but he felt he could work through the pain as 
he had worked through pain in the past. Physical examination on this date revealed tenderness in the medial aspect of the 
knee, normal range of motion, and crepitus.  Petitioner’s gait was noted to be antalgic, he walked with a limp. The 
diagnosis was a right knee strain.  Treatment included OTC Naproxen, Fast Freeze, a knee brace, and hot/cold therapy.  
He was instructed on self-care exercises and returned to work without restrictions, with a follow-up scheduled for April 
12, 2017. (PX 2 p. 1,2) 
On April 12, 2017, Petitioner again saw PA Droege at IWIRC, reported his symptoms to be improved, but said he 
had continued pain on both sides and in the back of the knee, He said when he walked or climbed stairs, his pain was 7/10. 
He said he had been wearing the brace, but it still felt like his knee might give out on him. Physical examination showed 
mild tenderness and a positive McMurray's test, so an MRI of the right knee was ordered. Petitioner was to continue the 
same treatment recommended at his first visit. He was again returned to work without restrictions, and another follow-up 
appointment was scheduled for April 20, 2017. (PX 2 p. 3,4) 
PA Droege saw Petitioner again on April 20, 2017. Petitioner advised her of persistent pain, 5-6/10, particularly 
on both sides of the knee and when walking on uneven ground or climbing stairs. He was wearing the brace except when 
he slept. He continued to have a slight limp on the right. Physical examination continued to reveal mild tenderness and a 
positive McMurray's test.  His MRI was scheduled for April 24, 2017, and he was to continue with the previously 
prescribed treatments, return to work without restrictions, and was given a follow-up appointment for April 26, 2017. (PX 
2 p. 5,6) 
An MRI of the right knee was performed on April 24, 2017, and was interpreted to show tricompartmental 
arthritis with extensive full-thickness cartilage loss in the lateral aspect of the patellofemoral compartment. Both the 
lateral and medial menisci were observed to be torn, with a nondisplaced root tear of the posterior horn of the lateral 
meniscus and a shallow inferior articular surface tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Chronic partial-
thickness tears of anterior cruciate ligament was seen, The proximal patellar tendon had significant tendinopathy with 
mild partial-thickness tearing, and the medial collateral ligament also appeared to have chronic partial-thickness tearing. 
(PX 3 p. 1,2) 
On April 26, 2017, Petitioner was again seen at IWIRC. The record does not reflect who saw Petitioner on this 
date. Petitioner noted that while he was better than on his first visit, he was unchanged since his last visit, with 3-4/10 
pain.  Physical examination revealed tenderness in the posterior leg but no low back or buttock pain. The MRI results 
were reviewed, and whoever saw Petitioner on this date wrote that Petitioner’s meniscal tears were not consistent with 
26IWCC0134

8 
 
Petitioner’s mechanism of injury and were not caused or aggravated by work. That unknown examiner assessed 
Petitioner’s right knee strain as having resolved, and Petitioner was released from IWIRC medical care, and told to follow 
up with his primary care physician for severe degenerative joint disease.  He again released to return to work without 
restrictions. (PX 2 p. 7) 
Petitioner was evaluated for right knee pain on June 14, 2017, by Dr. Merkley. He reported having no prior knee 
issues until he injured it while moving a rack of 400 chairs at Woodruff High School.  Petitioner said his pain was located 
in the anterior and medial aspects of the knee, and that he had developed swelling within a day of the onset of pain. 
Petitioner rated his pain as 4/10, and said it was aggravated by twisting, turning, stair climbing, and was accompanied by 
painful catching. On physical examination, Petitioner was noted to have trace effusion, retropatellar crepitation, and 
tenderness in the posterior and medial joint lines.  Tests revealed mild positive patellar thrust, pain with McMurray's test 
medially, and trace anterior drawer and Lachman's tests.  X-rays of both knees revealed mild patellofemoral degenerative 
changes in the right knee, with no joint space narrowing. Dr. Merkley’s radiographic impression was that of mild 
patellofemoral degenerative changes of the right knee.  Dr. Merkley made an incidental note of a complete loss of the 
medial tibial femoral compartment of the left knee. Dr. Merkley’s overall impression on this date was right knee synovitis, 
exacerbation of degenerative medial meniscus tear of the right knee, and exacerbation of patellofemoral chondrosis or the 
right knee. Dr. Merkley felt Petitioner’s symptoms were consistent with his meniscus tear and were also somewhat from 
the patellofemoral chondrosis as well. He stated that while these were most likely degenerative in nature, they had been 
exacerbated at work as Petitioner reported no previous problems with the knee. He recommended arthroscopy with partial 
medial meniscectomy and patellofemoral debridement as a treatment option. The procedure could be scheduled electively 
if Mr. Mayes decided to proceed. (PX 4 p. 1,2) 
No treatment records for the period from June 14, 2017, to October 16, 2018 were introduced into evidence, and 
Petitioner testified he did not believe he received treatment for his knees between those dates.  
Post-Accident records: 
Petitioner was seen by Nurse Practitioner (NP) Leas at IWIRC on October 16, 2018, for injuries sustained on 
October 15, 2018, after falling from a ladder at work.  Petitioner gave a history of trying to stop his fall with his right 
hand, and of hitting his left hand and arm on a ledge during the fall. He said he landed on both feet. He complained of 
pain in the area of the left trapezius muscle on his neck. He said his left hand had intermittent numbness and tingling, 
especially in the 3rd and 4th fingers. He said the bottoms of both feet were sore and tender.  He rated his pain on this date to 
5-6/10. He denied right hand and arm pain, but said his left and right shoulders were sore. He did note soreness and 
tenderness in both of his knees. His musculoskeletal examination of his shoulders on this date was negative. Both knees 
were examined and no abnormalities were noted. The 3rd and 4th fingers of the left hand were found to be mildly swollen 
and there was pain with palpation of the fingers. Range of motion of the fingers was found to be mildly decreased, with 
pain present. Petitioner was felt to have a cervical strain, a strain of his bicep tendon, forearm tendon, both feet left middle 
finger, and left ring finger. He was prescribed home exercises, ice/heat therapy, and Tylenol for pain management, was 
cleared to return to work without restrictions and scheduled for follow-up visits. (PX 5 p. 1-3; RX 9 p. 1-3) 
Petitioner was seen by NP Leas again on November 1, 2018. He reported no improvement in his pain, with persistent 
symptoms in his neck, left arm, hands, knees, and feet.  X-rays revealed degenerative changes in his hands, feet, and knees 
but no acute fractures. Physical examination revealed tenderness of the trapezius muscles on the left side, a limitation in 
cervical range of motion, mild swelling of the left knee, tenderness to palpation of the left medial and lateral knee, and the 
right knee had no tenderness, but pain with range of motion. It was felt Petitioner had a cervical strain of the left trapezius 
muscle, a left bicep tendon strain, a left forearm tendon strain, sprains of both feet, sprains of the left middle and ring 
fingers, and sprains of the right middle and ring fingers. He was prescribed Meloxicam for inflammation, referred for

ARBITRATOR CREDIBILITY ASSESSMENT 
Petitioner appeared to be cooperative and willing to answer questions posed by both attorneys.  He was not 
entirely successful in doing so, as the accidents, medical visits to doctors and actual treatment rendered occurred seven to 
nine years prior to the arbitration date.  He genuinely appeared to not know which knee or knees had previously been 
injured, and whether he had one or both surgically repaired in the past.  He readily admitted he had a one prior workers’ 
compensation claim involving his left leg, for which Respondent was entitled to credit, but even then he appeared to be 
unsure which knee that was. Much of Petitioner’s testimony in the days, weeks and years immediately following this 
October 15, 2018 accident was corroborated by contemporaneous medical treatment records.  Petitioner’s testimony was 
consistent with the contents of a Form 45 report created and signed the day after this accident. Respondent did not call any 
witness to rebut that testimony. The Arbitrator finds Petitioner to have been a credible witness.  
Both Dr. Akeson and Dr. Li were cooperative witnesses, answering all questions posed to them with no apparent 
attempt to evade the questions. While they had differing opinions in regard to causation, they both appeared to be giving 
their opinions in a truthful manner. The Arbitrator finds both Dr. Akeman and Dr. Li to have been credible witnesses.

Respondent presented no medical evidence or other information indicating that the Petitioner was under any 
active medical care for his left knee at the time of the date of accident or had received any medical treatment to the left 
knee in the nearly ten years between December 11, 2008 and October 15, 2018. Nothing in the record suggests Petitioner 
was having any medical problems associated with his left knee prior to the time of the date of accident.   
 
The medical records of Dr. Merkley and Dr. Luekemeyer as well as the testimony of Dr. Akeson support that the 
Petitioner’s having aggravated his pre-existing arthritis of the left knee in the October 15, 2018 fall from the ladder. 
 
Dr. Li did not believe Petitioner’s left knee condition was caused by this October 15, 2008 accident while falling 
off a ladder.  Dr. Li did note he had not reviewed medical records from Petitioner’s prior left knee surgery and did not 
know what surgery was performed at that time.   
 
The Arbitrator finds that Petitioner suffered an accident on October 15, 2018,  which arose out of and in the course 
of his employment by Respondent.  The Arbitrator further finds that Petitioner’s current medical condition of ill-
being,  severe medial compartment wear of the left knee, aggravated by the fall of October 15, 2018, is casually

treatment or complaints prior to the date of accident, and the medical findings of Dr. Merkley, and the medical findings 
and testimony of Dr. Akeson, both of whose opinions are given greater weight than those of Dr. Li, as they examined and 
treated Petitioner on multiple occasions, and, in the case of Dr. Akeson, actually viewed the condition of Petitioner’s knee 
during surgery.

As the accident occurred after September 1, 2011, the nature and extent of the injury must be determined through the five-
factor test set out in §8.1b(b) of the Act.  
With regard to subsection (i) of §8.1b(b), the Arbitrator notes that no permanent partial disability impairment report 
and/or opinion was submitted into evidence.  The Arbitrator therefore gives no weight to this factor.  
With regard to subsection (ii) of §8.1b(b), the occupation of the employee, the Arbitrator notes that the record reveals that 
Petitioner was employed as a custodian at the time of the accident, a position which requires physical labor, and that he is 
able to return to work in his prior capacity as a result of said injury, and had, subsequent to this accident been promoted to 
the position of head custodian.  The Arbitrator notes Petitioner has returned to work full duty.  The Arbitrator therefore 
gives  moderate  weight to this factor. 
With regard to subsection (iii) of §8.1b(b), the Arbitrator notes that Petitioner was 52 years old at the time of the accident, 
with numerous additional years of working possible. The Arbitrator therefore gives moderate weight to this factor.

With regard to subsection (iv) of §8.1b(b), Petitioner’s future earnings capacity, the Arbitrator notes Petitioner returned to 
his regular employment and continues to be paid pursuant to his union contract.  The Arbitrator therefore gives  no  
weight to this factor. 
With regard to subsection (v) of §8.1b(b), evidence of disability corroborated by the treating medical records, the 
Arbitrator notes Petitioner underwent a surgical procedure, a left total knee replacement. Dr. Akeson testified that 
Petitioner advised him on February 10, 2021 that he had returned to work and was tolerating work well.  and while he 
complained of having continuing pain in his right knee, no medical records reflecting medical treatment subsequent to 
December 7, 2022 were introduced into evidence.  His physical examination when last seen by Akeson on December 7, 
2022 was described by Dr. Akeson as fairly normal.  The Arbitrator therefore gives  moderate weight to this factor. 
Based on the above factors, and the record taken as a whole, the Arbitrator finds that Petitioner sustained
